_readme: Small config the agent reads/writes each run. artifactUrl is filled in after the first successful publish and must be reused (not regenerated) on every subsequent run so updates land on the same page instead of creating a new one each day.
pagesPublishScope: every run — uses GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN if set (scheduled cloud runs), else the local gh CLI
lastRunStatus: Weekly research run. No evidenceScore changes; one opportunity updated. entry-level-hiring-contraction-mixed-evidence stayed at 4 but gained a fourth contradicting-evidence source: a newly surfaced September 2026 Census Bureau working paper (CES-WP-26-61) finds that occupational AI-exposure measures -- the classification this trail's causal designs (Stanford, Census-Tucker, Federal Reserve) all lean on to identify 'AI-affected' workers -- predict firms' actual AI adoption only weakly (1-8pp effect after controls). Scored evidenceStrength 3 (indirect to the employment claim), below the trail's best (5), so per rubric 4e's non-stacking rule it does not add to the -1 downgrade already applied; evidenceScore arithmetic unchanged at 4. Independently of this finding, this opportunity's summary had drifted to six paragraphs, violating the rubric's 4-paragraph cap (a pre-existing error) -- rewritten from the full trail back to four paragraphs this run with no claims or [e:] markers dropped. No new opportunities founded. Product Management (still the thinnest role at 1) had a fourth consecutive run of leads investigated and closed negative (McKinsey case sketches with no disclosed methodology, PwC/WEF occupation tables that don't break out the role, Deloitte/Gartner/EY job postings that aren't organizational research). QA/Test Engineering (2): BLS's own Occupational Outlook Handbook entry for the role was checked and found to make no QA-specific AI claim; not admitted. Red-teamed all thirteen evidenceScore>=4 opportunities; no new threshold-clearing contradiction found for any beyond the methodological one above. BLS's dead-source streak climbed to 10 despite trying the recommended occupational-code framing. MIT Sloan Management Review, Deloitte Insights, and OECD newly crossed the >=6 dead-source threshold this run; McKinsey, Forrester, and Accenture Research (already above it) climbed to 7 each -- none read as genuinely dead, each surfaced real material that was either already captured or too weak to admit. Census Bureau BTOS reset to 0 on this run's genuine new finding.
pagesTokenPermissions: fine-grained PAT, repository access limited to sdm1130/ai-it-research-tracker, Contents: Read and write (Metadata: Read-only is added automatically). Nothing else required: main has no branch protection or rulesets, and Pages is build_type=legacy on main:/ so it rebuilds on push.

pagesPublishExitCodes.3: no credentials — skip and report mirror stale
pagesPublishExitCodes.1: real failure e.g. expired token — report loudly
